title: Event records carry agent run identifiers that the privacy guard blocks; committing events by default (#487) would publish them
description: 2026-10-20: committing board changes in the Kanbus repo was blocked by the local pre-commit privacy guard (leftblock with Pudicus gitleaks rules) on the new project/events/*.json files written by kbs comment and kbs close: the event records carry agent run identifiers and actor identifiers. Since PR #487 (kbs-65914cd1), kbs commit stages project/events by default and the repo no longer ignores it, so in a public repository these identifiers would be published unless the guard catches them. Decision needed from Ryan: (a) events never record identifying run values (store a stable, non-identifying actor label such as the configured agent name, or a salted one-way digest), in both runtimes, with a spec; or (b) events stay local by default and only private boards commit them; or (c) both. Also audit project/events files committed on develop since #487 for such identifiers before the next release to main. Until decided, agents commit project/issues only when the guard blocks events.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Decision (Ryan, relayed by the Cyclotron session 2026-10-20): keep actor_id and session UUIDs in Kanbus event records unchanged; LeftBlock allowlists them instead of Kanbus dropping or hashing them. No Kanbus code change. The allowlist work is owned by the LeftBlock implementation session.
